newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sale not to harm Stadshypotek - minister.
newsitem.headline: Sale not to harm Stadshypotek - minister.

text.p: A controlled auction of the state's 34 percent minority shareholding will not harm mortgage bank Stadshypotek, Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Friday.

"I repeat that the overriding aim for the state is to get the best possible price for the stake in Stadshypotek, and we believe an auction procedure is the best way," he told journalists after a parliamentary committee meeting.
"Of course I do not believe it could cause any harm."
Asbrink said the ministry had received several enquiries from parties interested in the shareholding, which the government wants to sell to an industrial investor.

The minister said he believed there was the possibility of an extraordinary shareholders' meeting of Stadshypotek, but added: "I am not about to engage in public polemics about Stadshypotek, It's bad enough as it is."
Asbrink criticised the board of Stadshypotek for announcing on Monday a planned merger with insurer Skandia without consulting him first.

The board defended its actions and said it had no intention of resigning over the issue. The minister representing the state's 34 percent holding has the power to call an extraordinary meeting to demand board changes.
